title: Sixty-four-bit integers nested inside structured content

source.clause: Annex A, property Content; §5 ("as defined in ECMA-404")
source.note: composed: ECMA-404 fixes the grammar of a number and leaves its precision to the implementation, and §5 inherits that by naming ECMA-404 for its types. This case asks that 64-bit integers nested inside a structured content survive a decode and a re-encode exactly — u64::MAX and i64::MIN, both past 2^53 and both inside 64 bits. It is what a JavaScript implementation loses by default, because every JSON number there is a double, and a second implementation has to carry such values as something wider than a double at every depth. The corpus deliberately asks for nothing beyond 64 bits: `ecma-432/12` is where that boundary is recorded.

notes: `ecma-432/12` is the corpus's other wide integer and it is the message's own content, which crosses a language boundary as a number. This one is *nested*, so it crosses as part of the structured value — and an implementation whose structured content is a parsed JavaScript object loses both digits before anything in the protocol sees them. `canonical_json` is where the case bites: the two digit strings must come back character for character, so an implementation that rounded 18446744073709551615 to 18446744073709552000 fails here and passes everything else.
